title: How the Capitalists Are Trying to Scare the People
author: V.I. Lenin
context: Published in Pravda No. 61 on June 1 (May 19), 1917, during the revolutionary dual-power crisis in Russia, this polemic refutes an editorial from the bourgeois capitalist journal Finansovaya Gazeta, which attempted to terrify the public into opposing workers' control over industry.
relatesToToday: Directly relevant for countering contemporary capitalist propaganda that equates democratic public ownership or workers' regulation with total economic catastrophe, individual deprivation, and totalitarian overreach.
keyTakeaways: Every major political transformation that transfers power between classes is fundamentally a social revolution; the February Revolution transferred power from feudal landowners to the bourgeoisie.
Workers' control over production, banks, and cartels is an objective, indispensable emergency measure needed to prevent catastrophic economic breakdown.
Socialist transformation does not expropriate the small and middle property of peasants and working people, but only expropriates the tiny oligarchic minority of monopoly bosses and millionaires.
Breaking the economic sabotage of a few hundred wealthy capitalists is sufficient to preserve production and secure the livelihoods of the vast majority.
